title: The Table Doesn't Care About Your Feelings
tagline: A ten-thousand-dollar buy-in, a final table forming, and a hand that's about to decide the whole tournament.

wake_up.text: Day two of the tournament. You're mid-pack in chips, well-rested, and the field has thinned considerably overnight.

choices.text: Review your notes on today's likely opponents
Skip the prep and trust your instincts today

breakfast.text: A proper breakfast before a twelve-hour day at the table, or a quick one to get to the room early and watch the room fill in.

choices.text: Take the time to eat a real breakfast
Grab something quick and get to the room early

random_moment.text: The hour before play resumes has its own texture in a room like this — a little different every day.

choices.text: A friendly player from an earlier table wishes you luck
A noisy group of spectators sets up right behind your table
You draw a favorable seat for the morning session

morning_session.text: Play resumes. The morning is quiet, a few small pots, nothing that tests you yet. The field keeps shrinking around you.

choices.text: Play tight and conserve chips through the quiet stretch
Look actively for spots to build your stack

bubble_approaching.text: The money bubble is close — the next elimination means everyone left cashes. Play tightens noticeably around the table.

choices.text: Apply pressure on the shorter stacks while they're playing scared
Coast through the bubble and let others take the risk

afternoon_session.text: You're through the bubble and building a real stack. The final table is starting to feel possible instead of theoretical.

choices.text: Keep playing

massive_hand.text: A hand develops that could double you into serious final-table contention — or send you home entirely. Your opponent, a tight player all day, just made an aggressive bet that doesn't fit their pattern. Everything you've read about them says this is either a monster hand or a huge bluff, and you have maybe thirty seconds to decide.

choices.text: Call, trusting your read that this is a bluff
Fold and preserve your stack for a clearer spot later
Raise back and put the decision on them instead
Take your full time bank to think it through completely

hand_outcome_call.text: The read was right — it was a bluff, and the call doubles your stack right when it matters most. Your table image just changed completely.

choices.text: Bank the chips and keep playing

hand_outcome_fold.text: You fold, and never find out what they had — the disciplined, unglamorous choice that keeps you alive without the swing either way. Sometimes the best decision is the one nobody remembers.

choices.text: Keep playing

hand_outcome_raise.text: The re-raise forces a fold from your opponent — you take down a healthy pot without ever needing to know if your read was right, which is its own kind of clean win.

choices.text: Keep playing

hand_outcome_tank.text: The extra time lets you notice a small tell you'd have missed rushing — enough to make a confident, correct fold, saving your stack for a cleaner spot.

choices.text: Keep playing

final_table_bubble.text: One elimination away from the final table. The room's energy shifts entirely — everyone left can feel how close it is.

choices.text: Play out the bubble

dinner_break.text: A dinner break before the final table plays out. Your body's running on adrenaline more than the actual meal in front of you.

choices.text: Eat properly and rest for the final stretch
Study your remaining opponents instead of resting

final_table.text: The final table. Cameras, a rail full of spectators, and a stack that puts you in genuine contention for the win.

choices.text: Play the final table

end_shift.text: The final table plays out late into the night. Win or bust, the tournament is over, and there's nothing left to do about it now.

choices.text: Cash out and head back to the hotel

triumphant.title: Final Table, Big Stack
triumphant.blurb: Every read today was sharp, every decision earned. This is the run other players will remember you for.

steady_hand.title: Deep Run
steady_hand.blurb: Disciplined, patient play the whole way through — no drama, just consistently good decisions.

ordinary_day.title: Cashed, Nothing More
ordinary_day.blurb: A solid day at the table. You cashed. Tomorrow there's another tournament exactly like it.

burned_out.title: Running on Fumes
burned_out.blurb: You made it through the day, but you're not sure how. Hand after hand, this pace has a real cost.

written_up.title: A Rules Dispute
written_up.blurb: Something about today's play is going in front of the tournament director. The chips are counted. The conduct still needs a look.
